card.name: Linking words before infection or illness
card.fires_on: Small linking words and punctuation (to, of, who, a comma, an open bracket) in text about infections and catching illness, where an illness term is expected next. Common in passages about children, exposure and germs.

modes.label: Exposure and risk links
modes.description: Words like to, of, or developing right after exposure or increased risk, before an infection is named.
modes.example: Children in day care have an increased risk of middle ear infections. The increased exposure<< to>> other infected children increases your child's chances

modes.label: Lists of infection or symptom terms
modes.description: A comma or bracket opening a list of symptoms or infection types.
modes.example: After coughing<<,>> sneezing or blowing his nose

modes.label: Spread of disease
modes.description: A linking word after a disease is said to spread or be caught.
modes.example: mononucleosis (mono for short) is spread<< through>> contact with an infected person's saliva.

card.writes: It pushes the output toward words like sick, illness and sickness, and away from unrelated tokens.
card.plain: It fires on small linking words just before a sentence names an illness or infection, especially in text about children catching germs.
